Fourier analysis of the WMS signal provides the optimum approach for accurate and robust recovery of absolute gas absorption line shapes.

the use of first-harmonic WMS with Fourier analysis and the general correction function is an extremely powerful tool for the accurate and reliable determination of gas absorption line-shape parameters and, therefore, for the simultaneous measurement of pressure, temperature, and concentration in a wide variety and range of applications.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

we have developed an effective and robust method to recover absolute line shapes using the first harmonic signal of WMS, which is suitable for a wide range (modulation index and gas pressure) of practical applications.
we have presented a new and powerful method for line-shape recovery using Fourier analysis which is valid for a wide range and combination of parameters.
, in the presence of high modulation indices, the line-shape may be effectively recovered using first harmonic signals.
The main takeaway from our work is that

, for the case of a single gas species with a known pressure and temperature, the line-shape recovery techniques presented here can be used to determine the gas concentration from the first harmonic signal alone, with no need for the second harmonic signal or any other additional measurement.

, by using the full Fourier analysis, we can achieve calibration-free measurements of gas concentrations and pressures/temperatures with high precision and accuracy, without the need to use any external references or calibration gases.

, with a simple and inexpensive laser driver and a lock-in amplifier, one can recover the absolute absorption line-shape of the gas of interest and hence simultaneously determine the gas concentration and pressure or temperature of the gas.
